declared_readings: A marker or transition names itself and the clip or sequence holding it, because it is stored inside that record. A clip does not name its track unless the track's clip list changed: retime_hold pins that.

The work area has no id. It is written as a member of its sequence, so the footprint names the sequence and changes() has the WorkArea entry. A work-area edit, a sequence-marker edit and a duration change therefore share an entry and conflict. That is the safe direction, a false conflict rather than a lost write.

The sequence duration is derived from the clips and Folio validates it, so it never changes alone. It has a footprint entry as before and no change entry; existing tests pin change counts on edits that move it.

What leaves with a removed clip is listed after its Remove as ClipMarker and ClipTransition entries with after None. A clip marker or transition on an inserted clip stays inside its Insert, which carries the whole clip, and the footprint names it.
A marker handed to another piece by a cut is one removal on the piece it left plus the new piece's Insert.
schema_id on the three records is one token per schema and cannot differ, so it is destructured as ignored. The key ids are what the pairs were found by.

Members no planner writes (enabled, source_ref, track settings, sequence name, frame rate, order-only differences) are reported by name without values; the values are in the snapshot and the inverse. A planner that starts writing one should give it a typed entry.
Footprint ids stay one flat list of strings. NOT_INSPECTED whether Folio refuses a marker id equal to a clip id; the only effect of such a collision is a false conflict.
spec_proposals: STU-ARC-011 or STU-VID: state the footprint granularity of a timeline edit, and give the work area a property-level name so it need not conflict with sequence markers and duration.
STU-VID: state that a timeline edit reports a change list, since none of the module's clauses does.
nest and multicam commands: state whether their proposals carry a write footprint; today they carry none.
